title: Scoring server readiness wait: timeout errors must report the last ping failure and chain it as the cause
answers: Why does the scoring server fail to start with only 'Wait scoring server ready timeout' and no reason?
How do I tell whether the model server refused connections or returned an HTTP error during startup?
Where is the model serving readiness timeout raised and how is its exception chained?
body:
Path: Startup readiness polling for the pyfunc model scoring server (the local server launched for serve/deployment and tests). Each attempt calls the ping endpoint via mlflow/pyfunc/scoring_server/client.py:ScoringServerClient.wait_server_ready, optionally watching a subprocess handle for early exit.
Rule: Keep the exception from the most recent failed ping in a variable (last_error) instead of discarding it, and on timeout raise RuntimeError with a message containing the server URL (self.url_prefix), elapsed seconds, the configured timeout, the server PID when a process handle is passed, and '<ExceptionType>: <message>' of last_error. Raise with 'from last_error' so the cause is preserved in the traceback. Polling cadence, timeout semantics and the early process-exit RuntimeError are intentionally unchanged.
Symptom: CI and users saw only a generic 'Wait scoring server ready timeout.' message after the model server did not come up, with no way to distinguish connection refused from an HTTP error from the server.
Constraints: Applies to readiness waiting in ScoringServerClient. If last_error is None (no ping ever raised), the message omits the ping-error clause and no cause is chained. Do not change timeout or polling values when editing this path.
applies: Readiness/startup timeout diagnostics for the pyfunc scoring server client; does not cover request-time invoke errors.
says: Local model server startup timeout fails to explain why the server did not start.
Include the underlying HTTP error or connection refusal when model serving startup times out.
Model deployment health check timeout errors should show the server address and diagnostic details.
Diagnosing failed model server startup is difficult because readiness polling hides the root cause.
Show the last health check error message when waiting for model serving to launch.
search: Startup readiness wait timeouts in mlflow/pyfunc/scoring_server/client.py:ScoringServerClient.wait_server_ready must preserve and chain the last ping exception as the cause. On timeout, the client raises RuntimeError including the server URL (self.url_prefix), elapsed seconds, configured timeout, server PID when available, and the exception type and message from the most recent ping failure using 'from last_error'. If no ping ever raised an error, the message omits the ping-error clause and chains no exception. This applies only to scoring server startup diagnostics, leaving polling cadence, timeout values, early process-exit handling, and request-time invocation errors unchanged.
